item.text:
**Bottom Line**

Mostly negative. In 2024, Tshisekedi’s government showed repeated use of state power to suppress scrutiny: journalists and activists were detained, media outlets were closed, the state of siege concentrated coercive power, and emergency/court/military processes were used in ways that weakened independent accountability. I did find limited positive evidence of oversight and correction, especially around the Court of Accounts, IMF-linked public-finance reforms, and technocratic appointments, but those signals were narrower than the repression record.

**Accepted Claims**

- `DRC president Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations` | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty says the state of siege militarized daily life, military and police power was concentrated, and journalists, civil-society activists, and opponents faced threats, arbitrary detention, and judicial harassment. This is strong evidence that the state was used to neutralize scrutiny and punish critics. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6, 7B.5

- `DR Congo: Second Term Should Focus on Rights` | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights) | HRW says Tshisekedi’s first term ended with repression, arbitrary arrests, and little progress on systemic reform, and it calls for stronger institutions and anti-corruption safeguards. This supports a finding that independent oversight was not being protected in practice. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6, 7B.5

- `Media Freedom Under Threat` | Amnesty International | 2024-05-03 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/media-freedom-under-threat/) | Amnesty reports Congolese authorities closed a dozen media outlets and programs on charges like spreading false rumors and inciting revolt. That is direct evidence of administrative censorship to suppress reporting. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6

- `DR Congo: Authorities must immediately free detained journalist` | Amnesty International | 2024-03-08 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-authorities-must-immediately-free-detained-journalist/) | Amnesty says Stanis Bujakera’s detention was judicial harassment meant to chill criticism and free voices. This is strong evidence of punishing an investigator rather than tolerating scrutiny. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6

- `DR Congo's arrest of activists invokes deja vu of growing repression` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/dr-congos-arrest-of-activists-invokes-deja-vu-of-growing-repression/) | Amnesty says LUCHA activists were taken by security agents, held in unknown detention, and threatened and abused. This is direct evidence of state intimidation against civil-society monitors. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6

- `Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts - report` | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | [URL](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/) | Reuters reports a civil-society report saying CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement, with calls for investigation. This is strong evidence of weak transparency around a core public process and supports concealment/capture risk. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.4, 7B.6

- `More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN report shows` | Reuters | 2024-09-12 | [URL](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/) | Reuters reports prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people and sexually assaulting more than 260 women. This is severe evidence of state abuse and the absence of effective accountability control. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.2, 7B.6

- `Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes` | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | [URL](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes) | The presidency says Tshisekedi backed the Court of Accounts’ control function and the court credited his support with helping revive anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. This is the clearest positive sign that he tolerated at least some independent oversight. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.6, 7B.4, 7B.5

- `Democratic Republic of the Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes` | World Bank | 2024-02-28 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes) | The project emphasizes merit-based recruitment, stronger information systems, and decentralized planning. This is limited but real evidence of a rules-based administrative approach rather than pure political shielding. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.6, 7B.5

- `DRC: 2024 Article IV Consultation, Sixth Review...` | IMF | 2024-07-03 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | IMF says the authorities cleaned up the civil-service register with biometrics, improved revenue mobilization, and maintained spending controls, though reforms were slow. This is limited positive evidence that some institutions were being corrected rather than hidden from oversight. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.6, 7B.5, 7B.4

- `DRC reaches agreement on ECF and RSF arrangements` | IMF | 2024-11-13 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | The IMF package calls for stronger treasury procedures, spending-chain controls, governance, transparency, and better customs enforcement. This is a real pro-accountability signal, but it is programmatic rather than proof of deep political restraint. | IDs: 7B.7; also 7B.6, 7B.5, 7B.4

**Search Gap**

- I did not find strong 2024 reporting directly proving or disproving a hidden personal-fraud scheme by Tshisekedi himself, such as a specific bribery case, secret foundation, or named asset concealment.
- The best evidence is indirect but still substantial: repression of journalists and activists, opaque election finance, weak judicial trust, and emergency-style concentration of power.
- On balance, the record supports “uses state power to suppress scrutiny and weaken accountability” more than “cleanly tolerates independent investigation.”
